title: fix(update): recover misplaced duplicate agent databases
body:
Refs #144689 (the separate per-agent startup isolation design; this PR does not close it).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users updating an older multi-agent installation could remain stuck in Doctor when one agent directory contained a byte copy of another agent's database. Repeated `doctor --fix` runs refused the entire migration and left the Gateway unable to start. Context: Discord support report 2026-09-10.

## Why This Change Was Made

The accepted repair scope is strict duplicate recovery: before either database migrates, Doctor verifies the complete database file sets and archive dependencies, checkpoints under its existing maintenance lease, and rechecks byte equality. It preserves the misplaced copy through the existing `.corrupt-<timestamp>` recovery owner, clears the stale registration, and lets the agent acquire a fresh store. Startup preflight consumes this recovered state; it has no separate recovery path.

Divergent or unverified copies remain refused and preserved. Doctor gives the owning agent, exact path, and an explicit operator quarantine command, while continuing independent state migrations. Repairs depending on the refused database, including deferred session repairs, remain blocked. Gateway startup with an unavailable agent is deliberately left to #144689. No schema, configuration option, dependency, or new recovery filename convention is introduced.

## User Impact

Updates can complete automatically when the misplaced database is a verified duplicate. Operators retain the preserved copy and see its location in the warning. Divergent histories are kept intact, and unrelated state repairs are no longer stranded behind that refusal.

Release-note context: Doctor now recovers misplaced duplicate agent databases during upgrades; divergent ownership conflicts retain actionable diagnostics and permit independent state repairs to finish.

## Evidence

- Before: the copied-database regression threw `DoctorStateMigrationRefusalError`; live `doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 1 after upgrading `main`, and Gateway exited 78 because `cleaner` remained unmigrated.
- After: the same regression passes, verifies the original bytes under `.corrupt-*`, opens a fresh `cleaner` store, and passes startup database preflight.
- Divergent regression: failed before because exec approvals remained unmigrated; passes after with the shared repair persisted, divergent history unchanged, and dependent steps explicitly refused.
- Guard tests preserve mismatched WAL, SHM, journal, and archive bytes and reject symlink/hardlink aliases. A WAL probe also verified that committed WAL contents survive recovery. A separate failing-before/passing-after regression protects against restoring sidecars after maintenance authority is lost.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.owner-mismatch.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.agent-owner-recovery.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-recovery-files.test.ts`: 10 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.agent-owner-recovery.test.ts src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.test.ts`: 7 guard tests and 239 existing session recovery tests passed. Existing media migration and generic migration-refusal sibling tests also passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` and `git diff --check`: passed. This includes core/test type checks, changed-file lint, import-cycle and storage guards. The assertion baseline shrinks only for the two removed legacy casts.
- `pnpm check:architecture`: passed after CI identified a duplicate raw SQLite checkpoint query. Recovery now reuses the existing Doctor checkpoint owner; no raw-query allowlist or suppression was added.
- Codex autoreview: clean through P1, including the CI fix.
- Live isolated state with a legacy `agents.list` roster and a Windows-like path containing a space: Doctor completed with exit 0 and the recovery warning; `pnpm openclaw gateway run --port 28741` returned `/readyz` with `ready: true` and `failing: []`. The task-owned Gateway was then stopped cleanly.

The live run was on macOS; the older-schema fixture is not an exact Windows 2026.7.2 installation. The remote did not provide the historical tag. Service repair was externally managed and all application state was isolated from the host Gateway.

Strict byte equality deliberately excludes copies that differ only because an earlier Doctor attempt already migrated the owner. Those copies retain the explicit operator recovery path rather than being treated as proven duplicates.

The pre-fix CI run on `92a01c98d0abb838c7d625e7be4b356f8ce7cd12` encountered the unrelated memory FTS fixture failure (repaired upstream in #144761) and profiler-help timeout recorded in [run 34568581840](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34568581840). Current-head CI will be verified before landing.

ClawSweeper's shared-directory preservation finding is addressed: a refused database now adds its archive directory to the existing file-only migration exclusion set. A healthy database can still migrate, while the refused database and shared legacy archive retain their exact bytes. This restores the established refusal contract without changing storage or recovery policy.

Additional regression evidence:

- Before the fix, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.owner-mismatch.test.ts` failed at the shared archive byte-preservation assertion: 1 failed, 2 passed. The healthy database had upgraded and the refused database itself was unchanged; the file-only media pass had rewritten the archive.
- After the fix, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.owner-mismatch.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.agent-owner-recovery.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-recovery-files.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.archives.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.canonical-archives.test.ts` passed: 5 files, 23 tests.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` and `git diff --check` passed for the fixup; the independent local-delta Codex autoreview was scoped-clean through P1.

Migration and upgrade compatibility confirmation: the accepted maintainer scope is duplicate-only recovery through the existing Doctor maintenance and recovery owners. The seeded older-schema upgrade completed Doctor and real Gateway readiness; the regression verifies preserved original bytes, an empty fresh store with the correct agent owner, and startup database preflight. Divergent databases and shared archives remain byte-identical while independent repairs persist. There is no schema/version bump, new persisted representation, or new retention convention. The follow-up fix restores the pre-existing directory-level refusal contract. Exact historical Windows installation proof remains the stated gap, and #144689 remains separate. This is the compatibility evidence requested in the latest ClawSweeper review, which found no remaining introduced code defect.

Final fixup head `ec7339978e7631c98849146322a94cc998d5be1d`: [CI run 34581211837](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34581211837) passed the native exact-head watcher (exit 0, effective rollup green, pending 0). The preceding run 34579984327 was canceled by GitHub concurrency in favor of a higher-priority request; it had 88 canceled jobs and no failed jobs. The watcher accounted for superseded check results. ClawSweeper revision 2 reviewed this exact head and confirmed the archive finding resolved, with no actionable code findings.
